beats.intent: ThinkSR addresses a mismatch between compact CTM thought and dense super-resolution output.
beats.claim: CTM's thought representation is compact; super-resolution needs a dense spatial field.
beats.narration: The central problem is that a compact thinking process must still produce a value at every spatial location.

params.headline: Compact thought must produce a dense image field
params.sub: A persistent carrier bridges CTM-style reasoning and super-resolution.

beats.intent: The method starts from a representational mismatch: compact thought is not enough by itself for dense restoration.
beats.claim: CTM's thought representation is compact; super-resolution needs a dense spatial field.
beats.narration: Compact thought can summarize state, but super-resolution asks for a restored signal across the whole image. The source compares CTM, a window-wise adaptation, and DQ-CTM to frame that gap.

params.headline: A compact state has to support dense spatial output
params.note: Figure 1 compares CTM variants used to approach this mismatch.

beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier while a compact thought process repeatedly reads and updates it.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: The method keeps dense features alive instead of asking the compact process to hold the whole image. The encoder creates the carrier from the low-resolution input. Windows expose local parts of that carrier to the thought process. Shared DQ-CTM ticks read and update those windows. The decoder turns the updated representation back into the super-resolved output.

params.headline: A dense carrier stays persistent through compact updates

beats.intent: The dense carrier is defined by encoding the low-resolution image, then windowing those features.
beats.narration: The equation makes the carrier explicit rather than leaving it as a diagram label. The low-resolution image is the input being encoded. The dense feature field is the persistent carrier. The windowing operation turns that field into window tokens for the compact process.

params.headline: Encoding creates the field, and windowing makes it readable

beats.intent: The end-to-end architecture joins encoder, windows, repeated DQ-CTM ticks, and decoder in one flow.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: The architecture is not just a compact module added at the end. Each named part exists to keep dense spatial information available while the shared ticks operate repeatedly. The decoder is downstream of the updates, so the output depends on the carrier after those ticks.

params.headline: The architecture keeps dense state in the path

beats.intent: Reconstructions are shown across ticks from T=0 through T=4, compared with bicubic and ground truth.
beats.claim: Reconstruction at T=0 through T=4 against bicubic and ground truth.
beats.narration: The progress figure shows the reconstruction state across successive ticks. It places those intermediate outputs against bicubic and ground truth, so the comparison is visual rather than only numerical. The source presents this as tick-by-tick reconstruction evidence.

params.headline: The output is tracked from T=0 through T=4

beats.intent: Absolute-error maps compare the same crops under one shared colour scale.
beats.claim: Absolute-error maps on the same crops, one shared colour scale.
beats.narration: The error maps keep the crops fixed, which makes differences attributable to reconstruction error rather than content changes. A shared colour scale makes the maps comparable across methods. The source uses this figure to inspect errors spatially.

params.headline: A shared colour scale makes the error maps comparable

beats.intent: On the reported five-benchmark average, DQ-CTM-SR is competitive with CNN baselines but below CATANet.
beats.claim: Competitive with CNN baselines; behind recent lightweight transformers.
beats.narration: The average score places DQ-CTM-SR close to the CNN baselines listed in the table. CATANet has the highest reported average at 29.482. DQ-CTM-SR reports 28.983, which is below CATANet but near CARN, IMDN, and RFDN.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is close to CNN baselines but trails CATANet

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR uses fewer parameters than CARN but more than IMDN, RFDN, and CATANet.
beats.narration: The parameter column gives the cost side of the result. DQ-CTM-SR is smaller than CARN at 1.129 million parameters. It is larger than IMDN, RFDN, and CATANet, so compact thought does not make it the smallest model here.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the table

beats.intent: The benchmark table ties the source's result claim to both reported measures at once.
beats.claim: ×4 lightweight super-resolution, average over five benchmarks.
beats.narration: The table reports both model size and average score, so the result is a tradeoff rather than a single ranking. CARN is the largest listed baseline. CATANet combines the smallest parameter count with the highest average. DQ-CTM-SR sits between those extremes on size and below CATANet on average.

params.headline: The result is a size-and-score tradeoff
params.note: Average is over five benchmarks for ×4 lightweight super-resolution.

beats.intent: ThinkSR's contribution is a method for using compact CTM-style processing while preserving dense spatial state for super-resolution.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: The source's main idea is narrow and concrete: keep dense state persistent while compact ticks update it. The reported result is competitive with CNN baselines, while recent lightweight transformers remain ahead.

params.headline: ThinkSR bridges compact thought with dense restoration
